items.name: Formal duality
items.statement_summary: The dual Sigma* of an elementary category-theory sentence Sigma is obtained by swapping composition order (g o f <-> f o g) and swapping dom with cod. Because the category axioms are self-dual (CT* = CT), whenever the axioms for categories prove Sigma they also prove Sigma*: if C |- Sigma then C |- Sigma*.

items.name: opposite category is an involution
items.statement_summary: For every category C, taking the opposite twice returns the same category: (C^op)^op = C (equation (3.1)). An interpretation of Sigma in C yields an interpretation of the dual Sigma* in C^op.

items.name: Conceptual duality
items.statement_summary: If a statement Sigma about categories holds for all categories, then its dual Sigma* also holds for all categories. Proof: Sigma holds in every C^op, so Sigma* holds in every (C^op)^op = C.

items.name: product
items.statement_summary: A diagram A <-p1- P -p2-> B is a product of A and B if for every object Z with maps z1 : Z -> A and z2 : Z -> B there is a unique u : Z -> P with p_i o u = z_i (i = 1,2).

items.name: coproduct
items.statement_summary: The dual of a product: a diagram A -q1-> Q <-q2- B is a coproduct of A and B if for every object Z with z1 : A -> Z and z2 : B -> Z there is a unique u : Q -> Z with u o q_i = z_i. Written A -i1-> A+B <-i2- B; the copairing of z1,z2 is [z1,z2] : A+B -> Z; the coprojections i1,i2 are called injections. A coproduct in C is exactly a product in C^op.

items.name: coproduct in Sets (disjoint union)
items.statement_summary: In Sets the coproduct A+B is the disjoint union {(a,1) | a in A} union {(b,2) | b in B}, with injections i1(a) = (a,1), i2(b) = (b,2). The copairing [f,g] : A+B -> Z is defined by [f,g](x,1)=f(x), [f,g](x,2)=g(x), and is the unique map with [f,g] o i1 = f, [f,g] o i2 = g.

items.name: finite set as copower of 1
items.statement_summary: In Sets every finite set A is a coproduct of copies of the singleton: A iso 1 + 1 + ... + 1 (n times) where n = card(A), since a function out of A is determined by its values on the elements. Motivates the notation 2 = 1+1, 3 = 1+1+1, etc.

items.name: coproduct of free monoids
items.statement_summary: For free monoids M(A) and M(B) on sets A and B, their coproduct in Mon is M(A) + M(B) iso M(A+B). Proved abstractly by combining the UMPs of M(A), M(B), the set coproduct A+B, and M(A+B) via the generator insertions eta. Consequence: the free-monoid functor M : Sets -> Mon preserves coproducts.

items.name: coproduct in Top (disjoint union space)
items.statement_summary: In Top the coproduct X+Y of two spaces is their disjoint union with open sets O(X+Y) iso O(X) x O(Y); for discrete spaces this matches O(X) = P(X) iso 2^X, giving O(X+Y) iso 2^{X+Y} iso 2^X x 2^Y iso O(X) x O(Y). Also: coproducts of posets by juxtaposition, and rooted posets Pos_0 with coproduct A +_{Pos0} B = (A +_Pos B)/(0_A = 0_B) identifying the two basepoints.

items.name: coproduct in a poset is the join
items.statement_summary: In a poset P viewed as a category, the coproduct of elements p, q is their join (least upper bound) p v q: p <= p+q and q <= p+q, and whenever p <= z and q <= z then p+q <= z.

items.name: sum types are coproducts in the category of types
items.statement_summary: Sum types in the lambda-calculus, formulated with case terms, are coproducts in the category of types defined in subsection 2.6.

items.name: coproduct of monoids
items.statement_summary: Two monoids A, B have coproduct A+B = M(|A|+|B|)/~, the free monoid on words over the disjoint union of underlying sets, quotiented by the least congruence identifying the two units with the empty word and collapsing adjacent same-side letters to their monoid product. Unit is the class of the empty word; multiplication is concatenation of representatives; injections i_A(a)=[a], i_B(b)=[b]; the copairing [f,g] : A+B -> M for homomorphisms f : A -> M, g : B -> M is the unique homomorphism with [f,g] o i_A = f, [f,g] o i_B = g, obtained by lifting [|f|,|g|] to the free monoid and checking it respects ~.

items.name: free product of groups
items.statement_summary: The monoid-coproduct construction also gives coproducts in Groups, where the coproduct of A and B is called the free product, written A (+) B.

items.name: coproduct of abelian groups in Ab
items.statement_summary: For abelian groups A, B the free product A (+) B need not be abelian; the coproduct in Ab is instead the direct sum on the underlying product set |A+B| = |A x B|, with injections i_A(a) = (a, 0_B) and i_B(b) = (0_A, b), and copairing [f,g](a,b) = f(a) +_X g(b) for homomorphisms f : A -> X, g : B -> X (that this is the unique homomorphism satisfying the coproduct UMP is left as an exercise).

items.name: coproduct iso product in Ab
items.statement_summary: In the category Ab of abelian groups there is a canonical isomorphism between the binary coproduct and the binary product, A+B iso A x B. The witnessing arrow is theta = [<1_A, 0_B>, <0_A, 1_B>] : A+B -> A x B, verified by computing theta(a,b) = (a,b).

items.name: coproduct functor
items.statement_summary: In a category C with binary coproducts: the empty coproduct is an initial object 0; the coproduct of two arrows is f + f' : A + A' -> B + B'; and these assemble into a coproduct functor + : C x C -> C, all obtained by duality from the corresponding product facts.

items.name: coproducts unique up to isomorphism
items.statement_summary: Coproducts are unique up to isomorphism. Proved by duality from the uniqueness of products, using that the dual of 'isomorphism' is 'isomorphism'.

items.name: coproduct associativity up to iso
items.statement_summary: Binary coproducts are associative up to isomorphism: (A+B)+C iso A+(B+C), shown by duality from associativity of products.

items.name: equalizer
items.statement_summary: In any category C, given parallel arrows f, g : A -> B, an equalizer of f and g consists of an object E and e : E -> A with f o e = g o e, universal: for any z : Z -> A with f o z = g o z there is a unique u : Z -> E with e o u = z.

items.name: equalizer in Sets (equational subset)
items.statement_summary: In Sets the equalizer of f, g : A -> B is the inclusion i : {x in A | f(x) = g(x)} -> A: any h : Z -> A with f o h = g o h factors uniquely through i via h-bar : Z -> {x | f(x)=g(x)}, uniqueness because i is monic.

items.name: characteristic function and Hom(A,2) iso P(A)
items.statement_summary: Every subset U of A arises as an equalizer, canonically via the two-element set 2 = {T, F} and the characteristic function chi_U : A -> 2 (chi_U(x) = T iff x in U), so that U is the equalizer of chi_U and the constant map T! = T o ! : A -> 1 -> 2. Conversely any phi : A -> 2 yields the variety (equational subset) V_phi = {x in A | phi(x) = T}. The operations chi and V are mutually inverse, giving a bijection Hom(A,2) iso P(A) (the powerset). Note: the Hom(A,2) iso P(A) conclusion and Proposition 3.15 lie on PDF 77; this construction is recorded here because it begins on PDF 76.

items.name: an equalizer is monic
items.statement_summary: In any category, if e : E -> A is an equalizer of some parallel pair of arrows f,g : A => B, then e is a monomorphism. Proof: from ex=ey put z=ex=ey, then fz=gz gives a unique u:Z->E with eu=z, and both x and y satisfy this, so x=y.

items.name: equalizers in posets, monoids, spaces; kernel in Ab
items.statement_summary: Equalizers in concrete categories are constructed on the underlying-function equalizer subset A(f=g) = {x in A : f(x)=g(x)} subset A with inherited structure: induced order (posets), subspace topology (Top), submonoid with restricted operations (monoids, inclusion is a homomorphism). In abelian groups, since f(x)=g(x) iff (f-g)(x)=0, the equalizer of f,g equals the kernel ker(f-g) = A(h,0) into A of the homomorphism h=f-g, i.e. the equalizer of h against the zero map.

items.name: coequalizer
items.statement_summary: For a parallel pair f,g : A -> B in a category C, a coequalizer is an object Q with a morphism q : B -> Q satisfying qf = qg, universal with this property: for every object Z and z : B -> Z with zf = zg there exists a unique u : Q -> Z with uq = z. Dual notion to equalizer.

items.name: a coequalizer is epic
items.statement_summary: If q : B -> Q is a coequalizer of some parallel pair of arrows, then q is an epimorphism. Obtained by duality: a coequalizer in C is an equalizer in C^op, hence monic there, hence epic in C (dual of Proposition 3.15).

items.name: quotient by an equivalence relation as a coequalizer
items.statement_summary: For an equivalence relation R subset X x X on a set X, with r1,r2 : R => X the two projections (r_k = p_k o i for the inclusion i : R into X x X), the canonical projection pi : X -> X/R, x |-> [x], is the coequalizer of r1 and r2 in Sets. A function f : X -> Y factors through pi (as f = f-bar pi) iff f respects R, i.e. (x,x') in R implies f(x)=f(x'), which is exactly fr1 = fr2; the mediating f-bar is unique because pi is epic.

items.name: Sets has all coequalizers
items.statement_summary: The coequalizer in Sets of an arbitrary parallel pair f,g : A => B is constructed by quotienting B by the equivalence relation generated by the equations f(x)=g(x) for all x in A; the quotient map is the coequalizer. Stated in prose with details deferred to an exercise (see Exercise 4).

items.name: presentations of algebras by generators and relations
items.statement_summary: In a category of algebras with free algebras F(n) on all sets and all coequalizers, an algebra presented by generators g_1,...,g_n and relations l_1=r_1,...,l_m=r_m is constructed as the coequalizer q : F(n) -> Q = F(n)/(l=r) of the pair l=[l_1,...,l_m], r=[r_1,...,r_m] : F(m) => F(n). The coequalizer forces the relations to hold in Q and satisfies the UMP: any algebra A with chosen elements satisfying the stipulated relations receives a unique homomorphism u : Q -> A. Worked example Q iso F(x,y,z)/(xy=z, y^2=1). Such algebras are called finitely presented.

items.name: presentations are not unique
items.statement_summary: Warning: presentations by generators and relations are not unique — the same algebra can have distinct presentations, F(n)/(l=r) iso F(n')/(l'=r') (e.g. add a redundant generator g_{n+1} with relation g_n=g_{n+1}). The finiteness condition is inessential: any sets of generators G and relations R yield an algebra F(G)/(r1=r2) as the coequalizer F(R) => F(G) -> F(G)/(r1=r2).

items.name: every monoid has a free-monoid coequalizer presentation
items.statement_summary: For every monoid M there exist sets G and R and a coequalizer diagram F(R) => F(G) -> M with F(G) and F(R) free monoids, so M iso F(G)/(r1=r2). Proof uses the free-monoid functor T = M(|-|) and the two-step bar-resolution diagram (3.2) T^2M => TM -> M with epsilon (concatenation multiplication in TM), mu = Tpi (fold using multiplication in M), and pi : TM -> M the counit; given h : TM -> N with h epsilon = h mu, the mediator h-bar = h o i (i = insertion of generators) satisfies h-bar pi = h and is the unique homomorphism, exhibiting (3.2) as a coequalizer of monoids.

items.name: coproduct via representable hom-isomorphism
items.statement_summary: (a) In any category C, show that A -c1-> C <-c2- B is a coproduct diagram iff for every object Z the map Hom(C,Z) -> Hom(A,Z) x Hom(B,Z), f |-> <f o c1, f o c2>, is an isomorphism (bijection of hom-sets); may be derived by duality from the corresponding product fact. (b) If part (a) was proved directly, derive the corresponding product statement by duality.

items.name: Ab has all equalizers
items.statement_summary: Show that the category Ab of abelian groups has all equalizers.

items.name: forgetful functor preserves the canonical monoid coequalizer
items.statement_summary: For the specific coequalizer presentation T^2M => TM -> M of a monoid M from the proof of Proposition 3.22, show that coequalizers of this particular form are preserved by the forgetful functor Mon -> Sets.

items.name: Sets has all coequalizers
items.statement_summary: Prove that Sets has all coequalizers by constructing the coequalizer of a parallel pair f,g : A => B as the quotient Q = B/(f=g), i.e. B quotiented by the equivalence relation R on B defined as the intersection of all equivalence relations on B containing the pairs (f(x),g(x)) for all x in A.

items.name: posets have all coequalizers
items.statement_summary: (Starred exercise.) Show that the category of posets has all coequalizers.

items.name: kernel relation, quotient, and generated equivalence relation in Sets
items.statement_summary: In Sets: (a) for f : A -> B, describe the equalizer of f o p1, f o p2 : A x A -> B as a binary relation on A (the kernel of f) and show it is an equivalence relation; (b) show the kernel of a quotient map A -> A/R by an equivalence relation R is R itself; (c) for any binary relation R subset A x A with <R> the least equivalence relation containing R, show the quotient A -> A/<R> is the coequalizer of the two projections R => A; (d) using the foregoing, characterize the generated equivalence relation <R> as the kernel of the coequalizer of the two projections of R.
